MS.note: For businesses already running on Microsoft. Built inside your tenant.

SETUP.name: Getting started with AI
SETUP.note: Config and training. No plumbing yet.

MSG.name: Talking to people
MSG.note: Anything you type more than once.

FIELD.name: Out on the job
FIELD.note: For anyone not sitting at a desk.

HOME.name: Life admin
HOME.note: The household side of the same problem.

items.title: Copilot licences people actually use
items.detail: You are paying for seats. We audit who has one, find the three tasks per team where it pays for itself, and run the session that makes it stick.

items.title: An agent that answers staff questions from your own files
items.detail: Policies, procedures, pricing, past projects. Staff ask in Teams and get the answer with the source, instead of interrupting whoever knows.

items.title: Documents generated from a form
items.detail: Engagement letters, contracts, proposals, quotes. Fill a form, get the finished document with the right clauses and the right numbers. Built on templates you already use.

items.title: Approvals that stop living in email
items.detail: Leave, expense, purchase orders, discounts. Requested in Teams, routed to the right person, logged, chased if ignored.

items.title: A shared inbox that sorts and drafts itself
items.detail: The info@ address that everyone half-watches. Triaged, assigned, and answered from drafts in your house style.

items.title: Meetings that turn into tasks by themselves
items.detail: Teams recording in, decisions and actions out, assigned in Planner with dates. The follow-up nobody had time to write.

items.title: A CRM with no new licences
items.detail: Client records, pipeline and follow-ups running on Microsoft Lists or Dataverse, inside the tenant you already pay for. Before you sign anything with Salesforce.

items.title: SharePoint tidied so AI can actually read it
items.detail: Nothing works until the files are structured and the permissions are right. Unglamorous, and the reason most Copilot rollouts disappoint.

items.title: The weekly report nobody has to build
items.detail: The numbers someone currently rebuilds every Monday, pulled and published automatically.

items.title: Invoices and forms read automatically
items.detail: Supplier invoices, timesheets, application forms. Data pulled out, checked, and pushed into the system instead of retyped.

items.title: A model tuned to one job, on your data
items.detail: When the off-the-shelf tools are not accurate enough for the task that matters most, we build the endpoint and keep the data in your Azure region.

items.title: What staff can and cannot put into AI
items.detail: A three-tier rule for your data — open, internal, restricted — written on one page, with the technical controls to back it up. Ten minutes to read, saves a notifiable breach.

items.title: The handover between two teams, fixed
items.detail: The point where work moves between offices, sites or an offshore team is where it gets lost. We map it, then automate the handoff and the status everyone chases.

items.title: Onboarding that runs itself
items.detail: New client or new starter: accounts, folders, checklists, welcome pack, reminders. One trigger, the whole sequence.

items.title: An assistant that knows your business
items.detail: ChatGPT or Claude set up with your services, prices, policies and tone — so it stops answering like a stranger.

items.title: Your five-prompt cheat sheet
items.detail: One page, written for your job, with the handful of asks you'll actually use every week. Fridge, not folder.

items.title: An hour, sitting next to you
items.detail: We use your real work, not a demo, until it clicks. Most people's "I get it" moment happens here.

items.title: Ground rules for what not to paste
items.detail: A short list of what should never go into a chatbot — customer details, bank data, anything covered by privacy law. Ten minutes that saves you a very bad week.

items.title: Talk instead of type
items.detail: Dictate a rambling voice note on the drive home; get back a tidy email, quote or job record.

items.title: One assistant for the whole team
items.detail: Same answers, same tone, whoever's on the keyboard. Plus you can finally see who's using what.

items.title: Replies that write themselves
items.detail: The eight messages you send over and over, drafted for you in your own words. You read, tweak, send.

items.title: Inbox sorted before you wake up
items.detail: A morning digest of what actually needs you, with drafts already waiting on the predictable ones.

items.title: Missed call, instant text back
items.detail: You're up a ladder, the phone rings out, they call the next bloke. Now they get a text in ten seconds asking what they need.

items.title: Guest messages, booking to review
items.detail: Arrival details, door code, wifi, mid-stay check, checkout, review request. All of it, on time, without you.

items.title: Ask for the review, every time
items.detail: The message you always mean to send two days after the job. Sent two days after the job.

items.title: Answer the same questions on autopilot
items.detail: A little assistant on your site or Instagram DMs handling opening hours, pricing ranges and "do you service my suburb".

items.title: Chase-ups that don't need remembering
items.detail: The polite second and third nudge, on a schedule, stopping the moment they reply.

items.title: One inbox for every channel
items.detail: Email, SMS, Instagram, Facebook, marketplace — all landing in one place, sorted, drafted, and nothing lost in a notification.

items.title: An enquiry form that asks the right questions
items.detail: Suburb, job type, timeframe, budget range. You stop having the same four-message conversation to find out it's not a fit.

items.title: Enquiry in, reply out, record kept
items.detail: They fill the form, they get an answer within a minute, and you have a contact list that builds itself.

items.title: Quotes built from a form, not a blank page
items.detail: Answer six questions, get a clean branded quote as a PDF. Twenty minutes becomes ninety seconds.

items.title: The follow-up ladder
items.detail: Day 3, day 7, day 14. Written in your voice, stopping when they answer. This is usually the fastest money in the whole catalogue.

items.title: Every enquiry in one list
items.detail: Gumtree, Marketplace, your website, the mate who passed on your number. One place, nothing forgotten.

items.title: A pipeline you can see in five seconds
items.detail: Who's waiting on a quote, who's booked, who's gone cold. A board, not a memory.

items.title: Ask for referrals without feeling weird
items.detail: A short, well-timed message to happy customers. Sent automatically, worded so it doesn't make you cringe.

items.title: Enquiry to paid, end to end
items.detail: Lead captured, qualified, quoted, followed up, booked, invoiced, chased. You do the actual work; the paperwork does itself.

items.title: Let them book themselves in
items.detail: A link that shows your real availability. No more six texts to land on Tuesday at 10.

items.title: The reminder that kills no-shows
items.detail: An SMS the day before and two hours before. Cheapest revenue increase on this page.

items.title: Cancellations that fill themselves
items.detail: Someone drops out, the waitlist gets offered the slot in order, first to reply takes it.

items.title: Your day, in a sensible order
items.detail: Tomorrow's jobs sorted by location with drive times, sent to your phone the night before.

items.title: Regulars booked in advance, paid up front
items.detail: Recurring slots, automatic invoices, and no awkward conversation about last month.

items.title: A diary that runs the whole crew
items.detail: Team availability, job allocation, customer confirmations, reschedules. One calendar everyone trusts.

items.title: Snap the receipt, bin the receipt
items.detail: Photo it, and the amount, date, supplier and category land in your books. June stops being a weekend job.

items.title: Job done, invoice sent
items.detail: You mark the job complete on your phone; the invoice goes out before you've left the driveway.

items.title: Overdue invoices chased for you
items.detail: A firm, polite escalation on day 7, 14 and 30. It doesn't get embarrassed and it doesn't forget.

items.title: Every property, every dollar, all year
items.detail: Rent in, interest, rates, strata, repairs, agent fees — tracked as they happen instead of reconstructed in July.

items.title: Your accountant's dream file
items.detail: One organised pack at year end: categorised expenses, receipts attached, income reconciled, notes on the odd ones. Costs you a coffee instead of a Sunday.

items.title: What are you actually subscribed to?
items.detail: A read of twelve months of statements, listing every recurring charge. People routinely find a few hundred a year they forgot about.

items.title: Kilometres logged without thinking
items.detail: Trips captured and categorised, ready for the deduction, without an app you'll stop opening in March.

items.title: Where the money actually went
items.detail: Bank export in, a clear picture out. Not a budgeting app you have to feed — a snapshot you can act on.

items.title: Contracts and agreements from a short form
items.detail: Fill in the client, the scope and the price; get the finished document with the right clauses in the right places.

items.title: What does this actually say?
items.detail: Paste in a contract, a lease, a quote or an insurance policy and get the plain-English version, plus what to watch out for.

items.title: A searchable memory of your own paperwork
items.detail: Every quote, contract, manual and email you've ever sent, answerable in one question. "What did we charge the Wilsons in 2024?"

items.title: Meeting or site call, written up
items.detail: Record it, get the notes, the decisions and who's doing what by when — before you've got back in the car.

items.title: Voice note to job record
items.detail: Talk for forty seconds about what you found and what you did. It becomes a proper written record, filed against the job.

items.title: How you do things, finally written down
items.detail: Record yourself doing the task once; get a clean step-by-step guide someone new could actually follow.

items.title: Your templates, tidied
items.detail: The nine versions of your quote template become one good one, with the variable bits marked up properly.

items.title: Listings written from the photos
items.detail: Upload the shots, get a listing that sounds like a human wrote it and mentions the things people actually search for.

items.title: Posts drafted and queued for the month
items.detail: A month of content from one conversation, scheduled, in your voice. You approve, you get on with your day.

items.title: One thing said five ways
items.detail: A single job, story or idea turned into a post, a reel script, a newsletter bit and a website line.

items.title: Google profile that stays alive
items.detail: Regular posts, photos and Q&A on your Google Business listing — the thing that actually decides whether locals find you.

items.title: A newsletter written from your week
items.detail: You send three bullet points on Friday; it comes back as something people read.

items.title: Before-and-afters, sorted and captioned
items.detail: The camera roll full of job photos becomes a tidy portfolio with captions, filed by client.

items.title: One page, every Monday
items.detail: What came in, what went out, what's owed, what's booked. In your inbox, on one screen, no login.

items.title: The spreadsheet, fixed
items.detail: The one you built in 2022 that everyone's scared of. Cleaned, de-duplicated, and updating itself from now on.

items.title: Watch something, weekly
items.detail: New listings in a suburb, competitor pricing, job ads, marketplace bargains — filtered, summarised, once a week.

items.title: Occupancy and income at a glance
items.detail: Nights booked, average nightly rate, cleaning costs, net per month, per property.

items.title: The whole business on one screen
items.detail: Jobs, cash, pipeline and marketing pulled from wherever they live into a single view that updates itself.

items.title: Job photos become a client report
items.detail: Photos in, branded PDF out — what you found, what you did, what's next. Sent before you're off site.

items.title: Checklists that file themselves
items.detail: Tick it on the phone, it lands in the job record with timestamps and photos. Handy the day someone disputes something.

items.title: Told when you're running low
items.detail: Stock and materials tracked against jobs, with a nudge before you're standing in Bunnings at 7am.

items.title: Hours captured without paperwork
items.detail: On-site time logged from the phone, rolled up per job and per person, ready to invoice.

items.title: One family calendar that everyone sees
items.detail: Work, school, sport and the in-laws in a single view, with the reminders that stop the 4pm phone call.

items.title: Meals planned, list written, order placed
items.detail: A week of dinners based on what you like, turned into a shopping list, ready to send to Woolies or Coles.

items.title: A budget that keeps itself
items.detail: Spending sorted automatically from your statements, with a plain summary once a week. No app to feed.

items.title: Nothing expires by surprise
items.detail: Rego, insurance, warranties, passports, visas — filed, with a nudge six weeks out.

items.title: Applications that don't all look the same
items.detail: Paste the ad, get a resume and cover letter actually aimed at it, plus a tracker so you know where you applied.

items.title: School admin, summarised
items.detail: The seventeen emails, notes and portal updates a week, turned into one short list of what you actually have to do.
